questions.question: If two forces of equal size act on a single object in completely opposite directions, what can we say about these forces?
options: They are balanced.
They are unbalanced.
They create a non-contact force.
They increase the object's speed.

questions.question: How is the resultant force on an object calculated when multiple forces are acting on it?
options: By multiplying the largest force by the smallest force.
By taking the sum of the forces, accounting for their directions.
By dividing the total force by the mass of the object.
By only measuring the force acting in the downwards direction.

questions.question: When the forces acting on a moving car are balanced, what happens to its speed?
options: The car will instantly come to a complete stop.
The car's speed will steadily increase.
The car's speed will steadily decrease.
There is no change in the car's speed.

questions.question: If a toy cart has a force of 10 N pushing it to the right and a force of 4 N pulling it to the left, in which direction does the resultant force act?
options: In the direction of the smaller force (left).
In the direction of the bigger force (right).
It acts vertically downwards.
There is no resultant force direction because they cancel out.

questions.question: If you increase the size of the resultant force acting on a moving skateboard, what is the effect on its speed?
options: The change in speed becomes greater or faster.
The skateboard will immediately travel at a constant velocity.
The change in speed becomes smaller and slower.
The skateboard will instantly reverse its direction.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the force of friction?
options: A force that only acts when objects are falling through a vacuum.
The force of one surface gripping or rubbing on another.
A force that always acts upwards against gravity.
The force that pulls magnetic materials together.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of adding a lubricant between two solid surfaces?
options: To increase the chemical energy store of the surfaces.
To reduce the friction between the two surfaces.
To increase the roughness and grip of the surfaces.
To make the forces acting on them become unbalanced.

questions.question: What is the standard unit used to measure forces?
options: Kilograms (kg)
Joules (J)
Newtons (N)
Metres per second (m/s)

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes categoric and continuous variables?
options: Categoric variables can take any value on a numerical scale, while continuous variables come in distinct types.
Categoric variables come in distinct types, while continuous variables can take any value on a numerical scale.
Categoric variables are always measured in newtons, while continuous variables have no units.
Both types of variables can only be represented by circle graphs.

questions.question: In a scientific investigation, what is the rule for a fair test regarding the variables?
options: We change all the variables at the same time.
Only the variable we are testing is changed.
We keep changing the variable we are testing until we get the result we want.
No variables are allowed to change at all during the test.

questions.question: Which statement is true about contact forces?
options: They can act when objects are far apart.
They only act when objects are touching.
They do not require any physical contact to slow an object down.
They are the only forces that can act in a vacuum.

questions.question: How do non-contact forces differ from contact forces?
options: Non-contact forces can act with or without the objects touching.
Non-contact forces only work when objects are in direct contact.
Non-contact forces can never cause an object to move.
Non-contact forces are always stronger than contact forces.

questions.question: What is drag?
options: A non-contact force that pulls objects towards the center of the Earth.
A contact force that pushes against objects moving through liquids or gases.
A force that acts only when two dry solid surfaces rub together.
The energy stored when an object is stretched or squashed.

questions.question: When drawing force diagrams, what does the length of a force arrow represent?
options: The time for which the force acts.
The size of the force.
The speed of the object.
The mass of the object receiving the force.

questions.question: Why is it more difficult to stop a heavy lorry than a light bicycle moving at the same speed?
options: Heavy objects have less air resistance.
The motion of heavier objects is harder to stop.
Friction does not act on heavier objects.
Heavier objects always experience smaller balanced forces.

questions.question: In science, how is a force defined?
options: A force is a type of chemical energy.
A force is a push or a pull.
A force is the speed at which an object travels.
A force is how heavy an object is.
